title: The Return Paid on Preferred Equity Being Revolved Under Membership and Patronage Equity
content:
What is paid here is the return on the equity being revolved and not the dividend the class pays on preferred equity still standing, and the board sets that return by how long the holding has been carried.

**Where the holding is long carried.** Where the class carries a dividend on preferred equity and the membership has stood on the books 20 or more whole fiscal years, the return is taken at 6 in the hundred.

**Where it is more recent.** Where the class carries a dividend on preferred equity and the membership has stood on the books fewer than 20 whole fiscal years, it is taken at 3 in the hundred.

**Where the class carries no dividend.** The class's own dividend rate on preferred equity is the rate taken, as the class schedule of Membership and Patronage Equity carries it.

## Boundary cases on hypothetical records

| Class carries a dividend on preferred equity | Whole fiscal years the membership has stood on the books | Return taken at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | 26 | 6 in the hundred |
| yes | 20 | 6 in the hundred |
| yes | 19 | 3 in the hundred |
| yes | 2 | 3 in the hundred |
| no | 26 | the class's own dividend rate |

The boundary is at 20 whole fiscal years, counted from the date the membership was accepted; at 20 the longer holding is reached and at 19 it is not.

**Worked.** Equity of 7000.00 drawn on yields a return of 420.00 at 6 in the hundred and 210.00 at 3 in the hundred, the figure rounded to two decimal places, and the return is worked out on that equity rather than on the pool share.
